question: What's the difference between the LLM and layout-based approaches, and when should I use each?

fetched_pages.title: Choosing an extraction approach
fetched_pages.content:
Guide to choosing between LLM-based and layout-based extraction methods

As you scale up and encounter document complexity, you can optimize extraction performance by choosing between large language model (LLM)-based or layout-based extraction methods.

Sensible recommends using LLM prompts for free-form, highly variable documents, and layout-based, or "rule-based" queries for structured, less-variable documents. In cases where either strategy works, Sensible recommends layout-based queries for the sake of fast performance and deterministic output. You can mix and match strategies since they're both part of Sensible's query language, SenseML. For example, you can fall back between layout- and LLM-based queries for the same document.

Comparison table:

| | LLM-based | layout-based |
|---|---|---|
| Technical expertise required | For nontechnical users. Describe what you want to extract in a prompt. | For technical users based on spatial layout. |
| Workflow automation | Suited to workflows that include human review or that are fault-tolerant. | Suited to automated workflows that require predictable results and validation. |
| Document variability | Suited to documents that are unstructured or that have a large number of layout variations or revisions. | Suited to structured documents with a finite number of variations, where you know the layout in advance. |
| Deterministic | No | Yes. Find the information using anchoring text and layout data. |
| Handles repeating layouts | Use List method. | Use sections for highly complex repeating substructures. |
| Handles non-text images | Yes, via Query Group method with Multimodal Engine parameter. | No |
| Performance | Takes a few seconds for each LLM-based method. | Offers faster performance in general. |

fetched_pages.title: LLM-based methods
fetched_pages.content:
Methods that use large language models for document data extraction

Extract free text from unstructured documents using large language model (LLM)-based SenseML methods. For example, extract information from legal paragraphs in contracts and leases, or results from research papers.

The following LLM-based methods are alternatives to layout-based methods.

| Method | Example use case | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| List method | "For each vehicle in an auto insurance declaration, extract the VIN, model, and year." | Extracts a list of data where you don't know how the data are represented. |
| Query Group method | "When does the policy period end?" / "What's the account number?" | Extracts a single fact or data point. |
| NLP Table method | "For each transaction in a bank statement table, extract the date and amount." | Extracts a list of data where you know they're in a table. |
